issues.legal_issue: A tenant cannot automatically set off excess rent payments against arrears as a defence to eviction for non-payment without electing adjustment and calling on the landlord to make it.
material_facts: The tenant’s contractual rent was 60 per month, but the landlord collected an additional 10 per month for 33 months; the courts found that increase was not permitted under the applicable rent-control law.
The tenant paid rent for the disputed five-month period late and argued that the excess payments should be applied to those arrears.
The tenant did not elect adjustment of the excess payments or call on the landlord to make that adjustment.
The courts found no proof that the tenant had paid the claimed advance of 300.
The eviction decree was sustained on the ground of default in payment of rent.
issues.conclusion: The landlord was not required to apply the excess payments automatically. Without electing adjustment and calling on the landlord to make it, the tenant could not rely on the excess payments to defeat eviction for rent default; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: Section 8(2) of the Bihar Buildings (Lease, Rent and Eviction) Control Act, 1977 provides that excess rent collected over fair rent is refundable unless the tenant opts to have it adjusted against past or future rent. Although that subsection concerns buildings for which fair rent has been determined or re-determined, the same principle applies to rent fixed by contract where the Act prescribes no different course. The tenant must elect adjustment and call on the landlord to make it; excess payments do not produce an automatic set-off. Sarwan Kumar Onkar Nath v. Shri Subhas Kumar Agarwalla and Smt. Draupadi v. Gorakhnath Gupta were distinguished because they concerned rent specifically paid in advance, and the former was confined to its facts. The Court did not need to decide the separate in pari delicto argument discussed with reference to Mohd. Salimuddin v. Misri Lal or the related authorities.

rule.if: eviction_for_rent_default and excess_rent_paid and rent_fixed_by_contract and tenant_did_not_elect_adjustment

predicates.eviction_for_rent_default: A landlord seeks eviction on the ground that the tenant failed to pay rent when due.
predicates.excess_rent_paid: The tenant paid amounts above the rent lawfully payable for the tenancy.
predicates.rent_fixed_by_contract: The rent payable for the premises was fixed by agreement between the landlord and tenant.
predicates.tenant_did_not_elect_adjustment: The tenant did not elect to apply the excess payments to rent arrears and call on the landlord to make that adjustment.

issues.definition: When eviction is sought for rent default and a tenant who paid excess rent under a contract did not elect and request adjustment, the tenant cannot use an automatic set-off to defeat eviction.
